newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban attack bottled-up Masood.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban attack bottled-up Masood.

text.p: Afghanistan's hardline Islamic Taleban militia launched an attack on Saturday on the mouth of the Panjsher Valley, where ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood is bottled up with his forces, witnesses said.

They said the Taleban fired volleys of rockets at Masood's positions high on the sides of the gorge which leads into the Panjsher and at least 50 black-turbanned Taleban warriors were seen scaling the rocky hillside heading for the ridge top.

Two rockets fired from inside the Panjsher overshot the Taleban's mobile rocket launchers by some 200 metres (yards), but the firing was the only sign of resistance from Masood's men, the witnesses said.
Masood fled Kabul last Friday after the Taleban made a lightning assault on the city and retreated to the Panjsher, which he defended many times against Soviet forces in the 1980s.
The Taleban leadership had told him to surrender or be expelled from the valley after they pursued him north from Kabul to the village of Gulbahar.
Gulbahar is at the mouth of the Panjsherr Valley.
